Command: Count fifty days from the sheaf offering
Summary: From the day the sheaf is waved, Israel counts seven Sabbaths complete — fifty days — to the Feast of Weeks.
Commandment: Count from the morrow after the Sabbath, from the day the sheaf is waved, seven Sabbaths complete, even fifty days.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The counting bound Weeks to Firstfruits and made the harvest season one long act of thanksgiving. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
